classification.difficultyReason: Model annual depreciation with a geometric sequence, locate an integer threshold by trial and error, and confirm it using logarithms with an inequality reversal.

content.prompt: A car originally costs $\$20000$, then at the end of every year, it is worth only 80% of what it was worth a year before. Let $W_n$ be its worth at the end of $n$ years.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write down expressions for $W_1$, $W_2$ and $W_3$, and find a formula for $W_n$.

answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}W_1&=20000\times0.8\\W_2&=20000(0.8)^2\\W_3&=20000(0.8)^3\end{aligned}$

This is a GP with $a=20000\times0.8$ and $r=0.8$.

$\begin{aligned}W_n&=ar^{n-1}\\&=(20000\times0.8)(0.8)^{n-1}\\&=20000(0.8)^n\end{aligned}$

$W_n$ is measured in dollars.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use trial-and-error on the calculator to find how many complete years it takes for the value to fall below $\$2000$.

answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}20000(0.8)^n&<2000\\(0.8)^n&<0.1\end{aligned}$

By trial and error:

$\begin{aligned}W_{10}&=20000(0.8)^{10}\approx\$2147.48\\W_{11}&=20000(0.8)^{11}\approx\$1717.99\end{aligned}$

The value first falls below $\$2000$ after 11 complete years.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use logarithms to solve part (b). When you log both sides, if the base of the logarithm is between 0 and 1, you must reverse the inequality.

answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}(0.8)^n&<0.1\\n&>\log_{0.8}0.1\\n&>10.31885\ldots\end{aligned}$

The inequality reverses because the logarithm has base $0.8$, between 0 and 1. The least whole number satisfying this is $n=11$, so it takes 11 complete years.
